brief: A practical analysis for operations leaders about customer-support automation. Show the operational trade-offs and avoid unsupported claims.
job_context: Fictional company Northstar Systems. Informative, non-promotional editorial voice.
inputs: No external research supplied; evaluate coherence and clarity from the document itself.
candidate:
Why Support Automation Still Needs a Plan

The team launched a support assistant after a successful pilot. It answered routine questions well, and the internal demonstration looked promising. However, running it across the whole organization introduced different challenges.

Those costs become a challenge. This matters because everything changes once it is live.

The new process will save money because automation always reduces labor costs. That makes the decision easy.

What Leaders Should Check Before Launch

That is why this matters to the future of automation.
